mainTopic: Salting on יום טוב, 'התירו סופן משום תחלתן' (permitting the end because of the beginning), and the dispute over store shutters (תריסין)
overview: This amud opens by finishing an earlier discussion. Spreading out a hide on יום טוב is allowed, because a hide can be used to lie on. Spreading out fats is not allowed, because a person might reason his way into salting them. שמואל rules that one may salt several pieces of meat at once even if only one is needed, and רב אדא בר אהבה used a clever method to salt piece after piece. Then a new משנה begins: בית שמאי forbid removing shop shutters on יום טוב, while בית הלל permit removing them and even putting them back. עולא explains that these are shop shutters. He teaches that in three cases the Sages 'permitted the end because of the beginning': the hide, the shutters, and a bandage in the מקדש. רחבא adds a fourth case, following רבי יהודה. The גמרא shows that each case teaches a new limit, and explains that עולא lists only cases with no live dispute. Finally, a ברייתא of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר disagrees with our משנה, a second ברייתא contradicts it, and אביי resolves the contradiction by dividing shutters into three kinds of hinges.

steps.title: Why spreading a hide is allowed but spreading fats is not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the difference. A spread-out hide does not look like processing, because it can be used to lie on. Allowing fats to be spread could lead a person to reason that salting them is just as permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, with the hide, the matter is not obvious, because the hide is fit to recline on. Here, with the fats, a person will come to say: 'Why did the רבנן permit this to me? So that it won't spoil. So what difference is there between spreading them out and salting them?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers an earlier question: why is spreading out a hide permitted, while spreading out fats is forbidden?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Spreading a hide has an innocent use, since people lie on it, so no one assumes it is being processed. Spreading fats has only one purpose: to keep them from spoiling. A person who knows that will conclude that salting them for the same reason is also fine, and that is a forbidden act.

keyTerms.meaning: the matter is not obvious / not clearly visible
to spoil / give off a bad smell

steps.confusionAlert: The worry is not that spreading the fats is itself forbidden work. The worry is about where the person's own reasoning will lead: from 'spreading is allowed so it won't spoil' to 'so salting must be allowed too.'
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common pattern in rabbinic rulings. A permitted act can be restricted when its only visible purpose would lead a person to reason his way into a real prohibition.

phrases.english: There (with the hide), the matter is not evident,
because it is fit to recline on.
phrases.notes: Lying on a spread-out hide is just an ordinary way of using it, not working on the hide.

phrases.english: Here (with fats), he will come to say:
What is the reason the Sages permitted it to me?
So that it will not spoil.
What difference is it to me whether I spread them out,
or whether I salt them?
phrases.notes: His reasoning would lead him to a forbidden act.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers a question on the previous amud, which contrasted the hide case with the fats case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases by whether the purpose is visible and where the person's reasoning will lead
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Spreading out the hide and spreading out the fats seem the same, so both should be permitted or both forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: The hide has an innocent use, but fats are spread only to keep them from spoiling, which could lead a person to salt them.

steps.title: Salting several pieces of meat at once
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה, quoting שמואל, rules that a person may salt several pieces of meat together on יום טוב, even if he needs only one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: A person may salt several pieces of meat at one time, even though he needs only one piece.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling about salting meat on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally on יום טוב you may prepare only what you need for that day. Here salting several pieces counts as one single act of salting, so it is allowed even though only one piece is needed. Adding pieces to the same act adds no extra work.

keyTerms.meaning: at one time / all at once

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:

phrases.aramaic: מוֹלֵחַ אָדָם כַּמָּה חֲתִיכוֹת בָּשָׂר בְּבַת אַחַת,
phrases.english: A person may salt several pieces of meat at one time,
even though he needs
only one piece.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the topic of salting fats and hides to salting meat for food on יום טוב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Several pieces of meat may be salted together on יום טוב, even if only one piece is needed, because it is all one act.

steps.title: רב אדא בר אהבה's clever method of salting piece by piece
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה would use a clever method and salt bone after bone. Each time he would choose a different piece as the one he wanted, and in this way he salted all his meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה would use a clever method and salt bone by bone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports how one אמורא actually behaved, going a step beyond שמואל's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל allowed salting many pieces in one act. רב אדא salted them one at a time, in separate acts, and after each one he said he preferred a different piece. Because each act was, on its face, for food he wanted that day, he ended up salting all his meat.

keyTerms.meaning: bone by bone / piece after piece

steps.whyThisMatters: This introduces the idea of הערמה, a clever method on יום טוב. That idea comes up in other places, where the גמרא sometimes allows it and sometimes does not.

phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava would employ artifice
and salt bone by bone.
phrases.notes: After each piece he would say he preferred a different one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds an actual practice that goes beyond שמואל's 'all at once' ruling to salting in separate acts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Salting piece after piece, each time for a 'preferred' piece, was practiced by רב אדא בר אהבה as a permitted clever method.
steps.whatToRemember: שמואל: many pieces in one act are allowed even if only one is needed. רב אדא: even separate acts, using a clever method of choosing a new 'preferred' piece each time.

steps.title: The משנה about removing and replacing shutters on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: New משנה: בית שמאי say you may not remove the shutters on יום טוב. בית הלל permit removing them, and even putting them back.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: בית שמאי say: One may not remove the shutters on יום טוב. בית הלל permit even putting them back.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins, with a dispute between בית שמאי and בית הלל about shutters on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי worry that taking the shutters off and putting them on looks like taking apart and building (סותר and בונה). בית הלל say it is permitted, and the word 'even' shows they go further: not only may you open the shutters, you may also put them back.

keyTerms.meaning: our משנה (marks the start of a משנה)

steps.confusionAlert: The word 'אף' (even) is easy to miss. It means בית הלל permit removing the shutters, and also go further and permit putting them back.

phrases.english: MISHNA: Beit Shammai say:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מְסַלְּקִין אֶת הַתְּרִיסִין בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: One may not remove the shutters on a Festival,
and Beit Hillel permit even replacing them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה with a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי forbid removing shutters on יום טוב. בית הלל permit removing them and even replacing them.

steps.title: What shutters is the משנה talking about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what kind of shutters the משנה means.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What are these shutters?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens its discussion of the משנה by asking for a definition. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling depends on what the shutters are. Shutters of a real building raise more serious concerns about building and taking apart than shutters on a movable stall. So the גמרא first pins down the case.

phrases.english: GEMARA: What are 'shutters'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of a key word in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What kind of shutters (תריסין) the משנה refers to.

steps.title: עולא: they are the shutters of shops
steps.stepSummary: עולא explains that the משנה refers to the shutters of shops, meaning the market stalls that were closed with boards at night.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: Shutters of shops.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא answers the question: the משנה is talking about the shutters that close up market stalls.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Market stalls were movable booths or wagons, not buildings, and they were closed at night with shutters. Shopkeepers would open them on יום טוב so people could get what they needed. Defining the case this way shows what בית שמאי and בית הלל are actually arguing about.

phrases.english: Ulla said: Shutters of shops.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the definition question in step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The תריסין are the shutters of shops (market stalls).

steps.title: עולא's list: three cases where the end was permitted because of the beginning
steps.stepSummary: עולא teaches a general rule: in three cases the Sages permitted the end of an action so that people would do the beginning. The cases are: spreading a hide for treaders, shop shutters, and putting a bandage back on in the מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: And עולא said: In three cases the Sages permitted the end because of the beginning. These are: putting a hide before the people who tread on it, the shutters of shops, and putting a bandage back on in the מקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא gives a general principle with three examples. The shop shutters from our משנה are one of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each "beginning" is something good the Sages want people to do: slaughtering for שמחת יום טוב, opening shops so people can buy food for יום טוב, and a כהן doing the עבודה. If the "end" were forbidden, people might avoid the beginning, so the Sages permitted the end too. This explains why בית הלל permit even putting the shutters back. Closing the shop is the "end" of opening it to sell food.

keyTerms.meaning: Their end because of their beginning. The end is permitted so people will not avoid the beginning.
Hide or skin of an animal
Treaders, the people who step on a hide as an early stage of tanning
Shutters of shops, the boards used to close market stalls
A bandage or compress placed on a wound

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think that the "end" is permitted because it is a small thing on its own. It is permitted only because forbidding it would stop people from doing the good beginning.
steps.whyThisMatters: This principle is the reason behind בית הלל's ruling in our משנה. They allow putting the shutters back because the Sages want shops to open on יום טוב.

phrases.english: And Ulla said:
phrases.notes: The same עולא who just explained that the משנה refers to shop shutters.

phrases.english: Three things they (the Sages) permitted
their end because of their beginning,
phrases.notes: The end is allowed so people will not avoid the good beginning.

phrases.english: and these are they:
a hide (spread) before the treaders,
phrases.notes: Beginning: slaughtering on יום טוב. End: preparing the hide for tanning.

phrases.english: and the shutters of shops,
phrases.notes: Beginning: opening the shop to sell food for יום טוב. End: putting the shutters back.

phrases.english: and putting a bandage back on in the Temple.
phrases.notes: Beginning: a כהן removes his bandage to do the עבודה. End: he may put it back on, even on שבת.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר עוּלָּא: שְׁלֹשָׁה דְּבָרִים הִתִּירוּ סוֹפָן מִשּׁוּם תְּחִלָּתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: עולא expands his explanation of the shutters into a general principle. It gives the reason for בית הלל's ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In three cases the Sages permitted the end of an action so as not to discourage the beginning: the hide before treaders, shop shutters, and replacing a bandage in the מקדש.

steps.title: רחבא adds a fourth case: opening a barrel or starting dough for the רגל
steps.stepSummary: רחבא, quoting רבי יהודה, adds another case to עולא's list: a person who opens a barrel of wine or begins selling his dough for the רגל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רחבא said that רבי יהודה said: Also one who opens his barrel, or begins to sell his dough, for the sake of the רגל.
steps.whatsHappening: רחבא adds a fourth example of the same principle to עולא's list of three.
steps.deeperAnalysis: During the רגל, wine and dough sold in ירושלים are treated as טהור so that everyone can buy them. The "beginning" is opening the barrel or starting the dough to sell to the crowds on the רגל. The "end" is that whatever is left after the רגל keeps its טהור status, so sellers will not be afraid to open up for the festival.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who reports the teaching of רבי יהודה
Also, adding one more case to the list
Dough, here for bread to be sold
For the sake of the festival, when pilgrims come to ירושלים

phrases.english: And Rachava said (that) Rabbi Yehuda said:
Also one who opens his barrel,
phrases.notes: He opens a barrel of wine to sell it to pilgrims.

phrases.english: and one who begins (selling) his dough
phrases.notes: He starts selling bread from his dough.

phrases.english: for the sake of the festival —

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This adds a fourth case to עולא's list of three.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person who opens a barrel or begins selling dough for the רגל is also a case of permitting the end because of the beginning.

steps.title: This fourth case follows רבי יהודה, who says he may finish
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that רחבא's fourth case works only according to רבי יהודה, who rules that the seller may finish selling the whole barrel or dough even after the רגל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this follows the view of רבי יהודה, who said: He may finish.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a short note identifying which opinion רחבא's case depends on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a תנאים argument about whatever is left after the רגל. רבי יהודה says the seller may finish it all as טהור, and that is the permitted "end." According to those who disagree, there would be no permitted end, so this would not be a case of סופן משום תחלתן at all.

keyTerms.meaning: He may finish, meaning he may sell the rest as טהור after the רגל

steps.whatToRemember: The rule "סופן משום תחלתן" means the Sages permit the end so people will not hold back from a good beginning. It explains בית הלל's shutters, the hide, the bandage in the מקדש, and, according to רבי יהודה, the wine barrel and dough of the רגל.
steps.confusionAlert: This fourth case is not agreed upon by everyone. It works only according to רבי יהודה's view that the seller may finish.

phrases.english: And (this is) according to Rabbi Yehuda
who said: He may finish.
phrases.notes: He may finish selling the rest of the wine or dough as טהור after the רגל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This limits רחבא's added case to the view of רבי יהודה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רחבא's fourth case holds only according to רבי יהודה, who allows the seller to finish selling after the רגל.

steps.title: Why teach the hide case if we already learned it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges עולא: the rule about spreading a hide before treaders is already in our משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The hide spread before the treaders: we already learned that!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why עולא needed to list the hide case, since the משנה already says it is allowed. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier in our פרק, the משנה records that בית הלל allow spreading an animal's hide where people will step on it on יום טוב. If the הלכה is already written there, עולא seems to add nothing by repeating it.

keyTerms.meaning: Those who tread or step on it (which helps process the hide)
'We already learned it' (in a משנה), a challenge that a teaching is unnecessary

phrases.english: A hide before the treaders,
phrases.notes: The first case on עולא's list

phrases.english: we already learned it!
phrases.notes: It is in the משנה, so why repeat it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for עולא's list given in Step 7
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's inclusion of the hide case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A teaching that only repeats an explicit משנה seems redundant.

steps.title: עולא's rule limits the hide case to animals slaughtered on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: Without עולא we might think the hide is allowed because it can be used as a seat. That reason would allow it even for an animal slaughtered on ערב יום טוב. עולא teaches that the real reason is to encourage slaughtering on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said that בית הלל's reason is that the hide is fit to recline on. Then it would be allowed even for an animal from ערב יום טוב. So עולא teaches us that they permitted the end because of the beginning. For an animal slaughtered on יום טוב: yes. For one slaughtered on ערב יום טוב: no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that עולא's rule is needed because it gives the correct reason, and the correct reason limits the leniency.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the reason were 'the hide is usable as a seat,' then any hide could be spread, even from ערב יום טוב. Since the real reason is 'so people will not hold back from slaughtering on יום טוב,' the leniency covers only an animal slaughtered on יום טוב itself.

keyTerms.meaning: 'You might have said'; introduces a mistaken assumption
'This teaches us'; introduces the real lesson
They permitted the end of an action so that people would do its beginning

steps.confusionAlert: The 'beginning' here is the slaughtering on יום טוב. The 'end' is spreading the hide. The leniency exists only to protect the slaughtering, so no slaughtering on יום טוב means no leniency.

phrases.english: You might have said
phrases.notes: Here comes the mistake we might have made.

phrases.english: the reason of Beit Hillel
is because it is fit for reclining on,
phrases.notes: Lying on it just counts as using the hide normally.

phrases.english: and so even from the eve of the Festival as well;
so it teaches us
they permitted the end because of the beginning:
phrases.notes: עולא's principle

phrases.english: one slaughtered on the Festival: yes,
one slaughtered on the eve of the Festival: no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the redundancy challenge of Step 10
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifying the true reason, which narrows the law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The hide is allowed because it is usable as a seat, so even a hide from ערב יום טוב is allowed
steps.terutzMaskana: The leniency exists to encourage slaughtering on יום טוב, so it applies only to animals slaughtered on יום טוב

steps.title: Why teach the shop shutters case if we already learned it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges עולא again: the משנה already says בית הלל allow putting shutters back.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shop shutters too: we already learned it ('and בית הלל permit even putting them back')!
steps.whatsHappening: The same challenge is now aimed at the second case on עולא's list. This sets up another explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה explicitly says that בית הלל allow putting shutters back, not only taking them down. So it seems unnecessary for עולא to list this case.

keyTerms.meaning: Shop shutters (boards closing the market stalls)

phrases.english: Shop shutters too, we already learned:
'And Beit Hillel permit even putting them back'!
phrases.notes: Quoting our משנה

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the Step 10 challenge for the second case
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's inclusion of the shutters case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה already permits putting the shutters back.

steps.title: עולא's rule limits the shutters case to shops, not houses
steps.stepSummary: Without עולא we might think shutters are allowed because building and taking apart do not apply to כלים. That reason would allow house shutters too. עולא teaches that only shop shutters are allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said that בית הלל's reason is that there is no building and no taking apart with כלים. Then even house shutters would be allowed. So עולא teaches us that they permitted the end because of the beginning. Shops: yes. Houses: no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that עולא's rule is needed to show the true reason, which limits the leniency to shops.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the reason were that the shutters count as כלים, so the laws of בנין and סתירה do not apply, then house shutters would be allowed too. Since the real reason is to let shopkeepers open and sell food for יום טוב, the leniency applies only to shops.

phrases.english: You might have said
the reason of Beit Hillel
is because there is no building with vessels
and no dismantling with vessels,
and so even those of houses as well;
so it teaches us
they permitted the end because of the beginning:
phrases.notes: Opening the shop to sell food is the 'beginning'

phrases.english: those of shops: yes,
those of houses: no.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא טַעְמַיְיהוּ דְּבֵית הִלֵּל מִשּׁוּם דְּאֵין בִּנְיָן בְּכֵלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 12 using the same pattern as Step 11
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifying the true reason, which narrows the law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Shutters are allowed because בנין and סתירה do not apply to כלים, so house shutters are also allowed
steps.terutzMaskana: The leniency exists to encourage shops to open for יום טוב, so it applies only to shops

steps.title: Why teach the bandage case if we already learned it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges עולא's third case: a משנה already says a bandage may be put back in the מקדש but not outside it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Putting back a bandage in the מקדש: we already learned that too! 'One may put back a bandage in the מקדש, but not in the country.'
steps.whatsHappening: The same challenge is aimed at the third case. This sets up the next explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A משנה already states that a כהן may put back a bandage in the מקדש even on שבת. Outside the מקדש it is not allowed. So עולא's listing seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: A bandage or poultice on a wound
The country, meaning anywhere outside the מקדש

phrases.english: Putting back a bandage in the Temple,
we already learned that too:
'One may put back a bandage in the Temple','
phrases.notes: Quoting a משנה

phrases.english: 'but not in the country'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the challenge for the third case
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's inclusion of the bandage case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה already explicitly permits it in the מקדש.

steps.title: עולא's rule limits the bandage case to a כהן who can serve
steps.stepSummary: Without עולא we might think the bandage is allowed because rabbinic שבות rules do not apply in the מקדש. That reason would allow any כהן. עולא teaches that only a כהן fit for עבודה may do it.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: what is the reason? Because there is no שבות in the מקדש, so even a כהן who is not fit for עבודה may do it. So עולא teaches us that they permitted the end because of the beginning. One fit for עבודה: yes. One not fit for עבודה: no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that עולא's rule is needed because it gives the true reason, which limits who may put the bandage back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the reason were 'rabbinic שבות does not apply in the מקדש,' then every כהן there could put his bandage back. Since the real reason is to make sure a כהן will remove it and do the עבודה, only a כהן fit for עבודה gets the leniency.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic prohibition on שבת or יום טוב
Someone fit to perform the Temple service

steps.whatToRemember: All three answers follow one pattern. Without עולא's reason we would guess a broad reason and allow too much. 'התירו סופן משום תחלתן' limits each leniency: a hide only from יום טוב slaughter, shutters only of shops, a bandage only for a כהן fit for עבודה.

phrases.english: You might have said:
what is the reason?
because there is no rabbinic prohibition in the Temple,
so even a priest
who is not fit for the service;
so it teaches us
they permitted the end because of the beginning:
one fit for the service: yes,
one not fit for the service: no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 14 and completes the three answers for עולא's list
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifying the true reason, which narrows the law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since there is no שבות in the מקדש, any כהן may put back his bandage
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a כהן fit for עבודה may, since the leniency exists to make sure the service is done

steps.title: Why add the wine barrel case if we already learned it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא aims the same challenge at רחבא's added case: a משנה already records that רבי יהודה lets him finish and the חכמים do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who opens his barrel: we already learned that too! 'One who opens his barrel, or begins selling his dough, for the רגל: רבי יהודה says he may finish, and the חכמים say he may not finish.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רחבא needed to add the barrel case, since a משנה already contains it. The answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: During the רגל, the wine and dough are treated as טהור. The משנה argues about whether the seller may keep selling what is left after the רגל. Since that dispute is already written, רחבא's addition seems to add nothing.

phrases.english: One who opens his barrel,
phrases.notes: רחבא's added case

phrases.english: we already learned that too:
'One who opens his barrel,
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה

phrases.english: or begins selling his dough
for the sake of the Festival,
Rabbi Yehuda says: he may finish,
and the Rabbis say: he may not finish.'
phrases.notes: The answer comes next

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same redundancy challenge to רחבא's case from Step 8
steps.kashyaTarget: רחבא's addition of the barrel and dough case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The dispute between רבי יהודה and the חכמים is already in a משנה, so listing it again seems redundant.

steps.title: Why רחבא's case still needed to be said
steps.stepSummary: Without רחבא we might think anyone may finish selling, even if he never started, because the רבנן treated an עם הארץ's impurity on the רגל as pure. רחבא teaches that only one who already started may finish.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: since the רבנן treated the impurity of an עם הארץ during the festival as purity, even someone who did not start may finish. So רחבא teaches us that they permitted the end only because of the beginning. If he started, yes. If he did not start, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 16. It shows that רחבא's statement teaches something new even though a משנה already records the dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mistaken reasoning is that the festival purity rule (טומאת עם הארץ ברגל) makes the wine and dough fully pure, so even someone who did not start could finish. רחבא shows the real reason is different. The רבנן let a person finish only to encourage him to start, so the leniency applies only if he actually started.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (introduces a mistaken assumption)
The impurity of an unlearned person who is not careful about purity
They permitted the end because of the beginning

steps.whyThisMatters: The principle הִתִּירוּ סוֹפָן מִשּׁוּם תְּחִלָּתָן appears in many places in ש״ס. A leniency granted only to encourage a first step does not cover someone who never took that step.

phrases.english: You might have said
the impurity of an unlearned person on the festival
the Rabbis made it like purity,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא הִתְחִיל נָמֵי,
phrases.english: so even if he did not begin, he may also finish,
so he teaches us
they permitted the end because of the beginning:
if he began, yes,
if he did not begin, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge against רחבא in step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא: shows the statement blocks a mistaken reason that would widen the rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because of the festival purity rule, even one who did not start may finish.
steps.terutzMaskana: The leniency exists only to encourage starting, so only one who started may finish.

steps.title: Why did עולא leave out this case?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why עולא did not include רחבא's case in his list.
steps.simpleTranslation: And עולא, what is the reason he did not say this case?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that רחבא's case is shown to be a real חידוש, the גמרא asks why עולא did not add it to his list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא listed cases where an action is allowed for a specific reason. רחבא's case fits that pattern, so it seems it should have been included. The גמרא wants to know what made עולא leave it out.

phrases.english: And עולא, what is the reason
that he did not say this?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוּלָּא מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמַר הָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on רחבא's case by asking about עולא's omission.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why עולא's list does not include the case of finishing the sale.

steps.title: עולא only lists cases without a dispute
steps.stepSummary: עולא only deals with cases that are not a מחלוקת. רחבא's case is a dispute between רבי יהודה and the חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: He does not deal with a case that is in dispute.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that עולא only listed cases where everyone agrees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רחבא's case, רבי יהודה says one may finish and the חכמים say one may not. Because there is a real מחלוקת, the case does not fit עולא's list.

keyTerms.meaning: He is dealing with / speaking about

phrases.english: He does not deal with a case that is in dispute.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: עולא lists only undisputed cases, and רחבא's case is disputed.

steps.title: But עולא's own cases are also disputed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that עולא's other cases are also disputes, since they involve בית שמאי and בית הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: But these cases are also disputes!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer of step 19. עולא's own list includes cases that בית שמאי and בית הלל argue about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Take the shutters case: בית שמאי forbid and בית הלל permit. If עולא avoids disputes, he should not have listed that case either. So the answer seems inconsistent.

phrases.english: These, too, are disputes!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that עולא only lists undisputed cases.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: עולא's own cases are בית שמאי versus בית הלל disputes, so his list is not free of disputes.

steps.title: בית שמאי against בית הלל does not count
steps.stepSummary: When בית שמאי disagree with בית הלל, their view is not treated as a real משנה position, so those cases count as undisputed.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי in the place of בית הלל is not considered a משנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the answer. A disagreement of בית שמאי against בית הלל is not a real dispute for practical purposes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הלכה always follows בית הלל against בית שמאי, so בית שמאי's view is set aside entirely. That is why עולא's cases count as undisputed. רחבא's case is different, because רבי יהודה and the חכמים are both live opinions.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not considered a (valid) משנה position

steps.whatToRemember: עולא lists only cases with no live dispute. בית שמאי against בית הלל does not count as a dispute, but רבי יהודה against the חכמים does.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean בית שמאי's words are missing from the משנה. They are written there, but they are not treated as a position one could follow.

phrases.english: בית שמאי against בית הלל
is not considered a משנה.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי בִּמְקוֹם בֵּית הִלֵּל אֵינָהּ מִשְׁנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines what counts as a dispute
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any disagreement, including בית שמאי against בית הלל, counts as a dispute.
steps.terutzMaskana: בית שמאי's view against בית הלל is set aside, so those cases are treated as undisputed.

steps.title: A ברייתא that disagrees with our משנה about shutters
steps.stepSummary: Our משנה does not follow רבי שמעון בן אלעזר. He says both בית שמאי and בית הלל allow removing shutters on יום טוב and argue only about putting them back. This applies to shutters with a hinge. Without a hinge, everyone permits.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our משנה is not like this תנא, as it was taught: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר said, בית שמאי and בית הלל agree that one may remove shutters on יום טוב. They argue only about putting them back. בית שמאי say one may not put them back, and בית הלל say one may even put them back. When is this said? When they have a hinge. But if they have no hinge, everyone agrees it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic. It points out that our משנה does not match a ברייתא of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר about shop shutters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In our משנה, בית שמאי forbid even removing the shutters. In this ברייתא, both sides allow removing them, and the only dispute is about putting them back. The ברייתא also limits the dispute to shutters with a hinge (ציר). Without a hinge, putting them back is just placing a board, so everyone permits.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה is not like this תנא
In what case is this said?

phrases.english: Our משנה is not like this תנא
as it was taught in a ברייתא,
רבי שמעון בן אלעזר said:
בית שמאי and בית הלל agree
that one may remove the shutters on יום טוב,
they argued only about putting them back.
For בית שמאי say: one may not put them back,
and בית הלל say: one may even put them back.
When is this said?
When they have a hinge,
but if they have no hinge,
everyone agrees it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the עולא/רחבא discussion and opens a new topic on the shutters dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, removing shutters is agreed to be permitted. The dispute about putting them back applies only to hinged shutters, and unhinged shutters are permitted by all.

steps.title: A second ברייתא says the reverse about hinges
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא says the dispute is about shutters without a hinge, and that hinged shutters are forbidden by everyone. This is the opposite of the first ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught: When is this said? When they have no hinge. But if they have a hinge, everyone agrees it is forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא that flips the hinge rule. This creates a contradiction with step 22.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ברייתא says hinged shutters are disputed and unhinged ones are permitted. The second ברייתא says unhinged shutters are disputed and hinged ones are forbidden. Both cannot be right as they stand.

keyTerms.meaning: But was it not taught (introduces a contradicting ברייתא)

phrases.english: But was it not taught:
When is this said?
When they have no hinge,
but if they have a hinge,
everyone agrees it is forbidden!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contradicts the hinge rule of the ברייתא in step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: The first ברייתא's rule that unhinged shutters are permitted by all and hinged ones are disputed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A second ברייתא gives the reverse, so the two sources contradict each other.

steps.title: אביי: three kinds of shutters
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that there are three kinds of shutters. A hinge on the side is forbidden by all. No hinge at all is permitted by all. A hinge in the middle is the case they argue about.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: When they have a hinge on the side, everyone agrees it is forbidden. When they have no hinge at all, everyone agrees it is permitted. When they argue, it is when they have a hinge in the middle.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי resolves the contradiction between the two ברייתות by splitting the cases into three.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A side hinge is like fixing a door in place, which resembles building, so it is forbidden. Having no hinge is just setting down a board, so it is permitted. A middle hinge falls in between, and that is the disputed case. Each ברייתא used the word 'hinge' or 'no hinge' to refer to the middle-hinge case, compared against a different extreme.
steps.whatToRemember: Shutters come in three types. A side hinge is forbidden by all, no hinge is permitted by all, and a middle hinge is the case בית שמאי and בית הלל argue about.

phrases.english: אביי said:
When they have a hinge on the side,
everyone agrees it is forbidden.
When they have no hinge at all,
everyone agrees it is permitted.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי פְּלִיגִי בְּשֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהֶן צִיר בָּאֶמְצַע.
phrases.english: When they argue, it is when they have a hinge in the middle.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי בְּשֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהֶן צִיר מִן הַצַּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits the cases into three categories so each ברייתא fits
steps.terutzHavaAmina: There are only two kinds of shutters, hinged and unhinged, so the ברייתות contradict.
steps.terutzMaskana: A side hinge is forbidden by all, no hinge is permitted by all, and a middle hinge is disputed.
